subject: Clarify DPA annex: subprocessors list & telemetry retention (PSA onboarding)
messages:
From: Darren Lee <darren.lee@crystalhealth.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@crystalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA annex questions for PSA onboarding

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we're finishing our PSA onboarding checklist, our legal team flagged two items in the DPA annex we need to clarify before signing:

1) Subprocessors: we asked for the full subprocessor roster scoped to telemetry and logging. The CSV you sent previously lists names and regions but not the specific telemetry categories (e.g., inference telemetry, anonymized usage metrics, request traces) each subprocessor processes. Can you provide a mapping?

2) Telemetry retention & PII scrubbing: the DPA annex shows a retention period of 90 days for inference traces; our SOC team wants to confirm whether those traces can contain PII and, if so, what automated redaction/hashing you perform. Also want to know if any subprocessor can access raw traces longer than 90 days (e.g., backups or archival systems).

We raised a minor compliance gap around cross-border copies for US–EU transfers used for capacity—are there any subprocessors/users in EU regions that receive masked/unmasked copies?

Can you loop in folks who own the subprocessor inventory and telemetry policy? We want short, actionable answers we can include in our security questionnaire.

Appreciate it — Darren
Security Program Manager
CrystalHealth

From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: Darren Lee <darren.lee@crystalhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA annex questions for PSA onboarding

Darren — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (privacy infra / subprocessors) and Neha (product security / telemetry). Well answer each point with the exact artifacts you can include in the questionnaire. High level answers below; Ben/Neha will add specifics and attach the mapping.

Summary answers (short):
- Subprocessor mapping: well provide a CSV mapping subprocessor -> telemetry categories processed (inference logs, error traces, aggregated metrics, observability metrics) + region of processing. Attached: latest roster (redwood_subprocessor_inventory_20260524.csv).
- PII in traces: inference traces are considered telemetry. By default we do not log full user inputs in plaintext for hosted customers; we keep a sampled, redacted trace used for debugging which has a PII-hashing step when configured. For customers who require default redaction we enable token-level hashing and prompt redaction prior to storage.
- Retention/backups: primary retention for traces is 90 days. Backups are encrypted and retained per region-specific backup policy; we do not retain raw traces longer than 90 days in production unless a customer requests a legal hold.
- Cross-border: we support region-pin and routing policies. When region-pin is not used, some telemetry may be routed for capacity reasons to other regions; those transfers are covered by SCCs and our DPA transfer annex. No external subprocessor receives unmasked PII beyond what is needed for operations; where needed we use pseudonymization and strict access controls.

Action items: Ben will attach the per-subprocessor telemetry matrix and note any EU processors that have access. Neha will add specifics on hashing algorithms, sample redaction logs, and the backup retention proof point. After that Ill produce a one-page Q&A you can drop into your SSQ.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Darren Lee <darren.lee@crystalhealth.com>, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA annex questions for PSA onboarding

Darren — attaching the CSV you requested. Quick notes in-line:

- redwood_subprocessor_inventory_20260524.csv (attached): columns = subprocessor_name, function, telemetry_categories (comma-separated: inference_traces, error_traces, aggregated_metrics, observability), regions_processed, contractual_restrictions, datasharing_scope.
- EU subprocessors: two analytics vendors process aggregated_metrics in EU (Frankfurt) for capacity reasons; neither has access to raw inference inputs. Both vendors process pre-aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry.
- Hashing/redaction: we use SHA-256 with a customer-specific salt for token hashes used in debug traces; our standard config drops high-entropy tokens flagged by PII detectors (emails, SSNs, credit-card patterns) and replaces them with stable pseudonyms.
- Backups: snapshots are encrypted with customer-managed keys where requested (KMS integration) and retention for snapshots containing telemetry metadata is capped at 90 days; immutable long-term archives do not include raw traces by default.

Ive also attached a redline of the DPA annex where we clarified carriers and transfers (dpa_annex_redline_20260525.pdf). If CrystalHealth requires stricter terms (e.g., zero-subprocessor access to telemetry), thats something we can discuss as an exception in the PSA (impact: longer onboarding and potential >10% SLA uplift).

-ben
Ben Carter
Privacy Infrastructure Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_20260524.csv (CSV listing 12 subprocessors), dpa_annex_redline_20260525.pdf (PDF with proposed language).
From: Darren Lee <darren.lee@crystalhealth.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@crystalhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA annex questions for PSA onboarding

Chloe/Ben — this is excellent, thank you. A few follow-ups from our SOC and legal: 

1) Can you provide a short example row from the CSV showing the pseudonymization field (we need to show the SOC how identifiers are replaced)?
2) For the SHA-256 hashing with customer salt: can you confirm where the salt is stored and whether CrystalHealth can bring its own salt (BYOS)? Is there a KMS integration path?
3) For the onboarding exception (no subprocessor access to telemetry), could you share a prose estimate of the engineering changes and timeline you referenced? Were evaluating whether to request that in the PSA amendment.

If possible, please reply by EOD Monday so we can keep the PSA signature on this sprint.

Thanks — Darren
